specs.rationale: A superseded PR push is stale; cancelling it frees a runner for the new run. A superseded main push still needs verification.

A tag is immutable; a second run for the same tag is a retry or a bug. Serializing is the safe default. The group carries `github.workflow` so a release run cannot share a concurrency group with a tier run on the same ref, matching the shape every other workflow's group follows.
Scheduled runs are the only run for their slot; cancelling one wastes its work. Push-triggered runs are rare and their inputs change infrequently.
Same as ci.yml: PR pushes supersede; main pushes do not.

The workflow is triggered by pull_request, tags, and schedule. Tags and schedules are the triggers whose runs must not cancel each other; a PR's superseded pushes are rare and their cost is bounded. The never policy is the conservative choice.
Tag pushes and scheduled runs are the only triggers; neither is superseded by a later run in the same way a PR push is.
Same as ci.yml: PR pushes supersede; main pushes do not.

Same as ci.yml: PR pushes supersede; main pushes do not. The tier is gated on push, so the policy's PR branch is rarely exercised, but the block is present for consistency with the other tiers.
A reusable workflow invoked by release.yml; the caller serializes, and the build itself has no supersession semantics.
A reusable workflow invoked by every tier; the caller serializes, and the cache itself has no supersession semantics.
